thread:
miriam: quick RFC follow-up — thinking we should add a lightweight 'wavefront' concept to rollout/pin metadata. goal: express gradual affinity ramps without adding a bunch of server-side orchestration.

akshay: curious, what's the shape of a wavefront? similar to cohorts? :thinking_face:

miriam: similar intent but encoded on the pin record. small example: a single pin can include a 'wave' list where each entry is {percent, start_ts, duration_s, route_hint}. clients or routing layers interpret it.

jess: can you paste a tiny example? makes it easier to parse tradeoffs.

miriam: sure — minimal example below (just illustrative):

```json
{"pin_id":"prod-alpha:v3","wave":[{"pct":5,"start":1769926000,"dur":86400,"hint":"us-east-1"},{"pct":25,"start":1769930000,"dur":172800,"hint":"region:all"}],"stability_hint":"canary"}
```

miriam: idea is routing/runtimes can honor pct and hint, fallback to base pin when unsupported. preserves single-record model.

reza: big win: avoids separate rollout objects + scheduled jobs. concern: clients need to evaluate pct + clock skew.

leah: also need a tie-breaker when multiple pins match. maybe a deterministic hash on tenant+request to decide inclusion in current wave. otherwise nondeterministic success rates.

akshay: agree re: determinism. also worried about metadata blowup: if we add lots of waves per pin, storage + transmission costs increase. but typical use will be 2-3 waves.

jess: compatibility story? old agents should ignore unknown 'wave' field, right? but older routing layers might not fallback correctly. we need a clear server-side fallback contract.

miriam: yes — spec: if routing cannot interpret 'wave', it must treat pin as full-affinity to the canonical model (i.e., pct=100). we flagged this to avoid accidental under-serving.

rez a: what about rollback fastpath? if a wave starts and we need to pull back immediately, can we push a zero-duration override?

miriam: propose 'grace_cursor' plus an optional 'epoch' counter on the pin. if epoch increments, client runtime invalidates cached evaluation and re-evaluates immediately. that covers emergency config flips without sweeping all caches.

leah: good. other nit: metrics/telemetry — we should add 'observed_pct' hints for the control plane to track actual routing decisions. otherwise ops won't know if a wave is effective. small extra field like 'telemetry_hint' or 'observed_bucket_key'.

akshay: sounds right. we should also think about the semantics for canary feedback: does "stability_hint" accept enums ("canary","stable","rollback")? keep it small.

miriam: propose enums: canary, ramping, stable, rollback. routing may annotate requests with the label it used.

jess: operational safety: what about tenant overrides? some tenants (enterprise) might want to opt out of gradual waves and pin 100% on deploy. need a tenant-level override precedence documented.

miriam: documented precedence: tenant_override > pin.wave > pin.base. that'll be in the RFC follow-up.

ops-bot: deploy note — new metadata fields will be accepted by control plane API as of next deploy, but runtime rollout clients will be gated behind a feature flag. See /deploy/rollout-wavefront.

reza: small perf note — our routing binary parses pin metadata on hot path. prefer compact list entries: pct as small int, start as epoch seconds, duration seconds. avoid nested object keys in perf path.

miriam: good point. will update example compressing keys to single letters if needed for wire format (e.g., "w":[{"p":5,"s":1769926000,"d":86400,"h":"us-east-1"}]).

leah: compatibility tests: add a smoke that simulates old client (ignore 'wave') and verifies fallback semantics (ensure 100% affinity if unsupported). also add a deterministic-hash unit test for inclusion boundary cases.

akshay: last thought — what about a 'weight_decay' knob for waves so that servers can gently shift traffic if they can't do exact pct shaping? e.g., server scales route score by windowed factor. optional.

miriam: noted. adding to tradeoffs section: precise shaping vs approximate rollouts on older infra.

jess: feels actionable. can you add a short PR with schema + sample migration plan? then we can sync with infra and runtime teams.

miriam: will do. I'll draft PR titled "wavefront pin metadata: schema + rollout playbook" and include the epoch/grace_cursor semantics and tenant override precedence. thanks all. :thumbsup:

leah: thanks — add me to PR for the telemetry bits.

akshay: tagging perf team and rollout owners in the PR.

miriam: (follow-up) open question for the board: do we want server-side enforcement of pct semantics (centralized throttle) or leave to clients? leaning client + runtime so control plane is simpler, but we should list tradeoffs.

reza: prefer client + runtime too — central enforcement adds big operational surface.

miriam: ok stopping here, will draft.
